title: Student visa (subclass 500): With this visa you can
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), With this visa you can: participate in an eligible course of study in Australia. travel in and out of Australia. work up to 48 hours a fortnight when your course of study or training is in session.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): How long you can stay
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), How long you can stay: Up to 6 years and in line with your enrolment.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Cost
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Cost: Cost concession. A lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens, eligible ASEAN citizens and applicants in the ELICOS and Non-Award sector who lodge a valid Student visa application. See About this visa. To work out what your visa will cost, use the Visa Pricing Estimator. The estimator does not take into account the other costs.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): You must
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), You must: apply online. apply from outside Australia unless you hold an eligible visa and meet an exemption allowing you to apply in Australia. be enrolled in a course of study in Australia and hold a valid Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) when we decide your visa. hold Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), or fall in one of the exemption categories. be 6 years or older. prove you have a welfare arrangement, if you are under 18. not bring family members (partners and children) to Australia, unless exempt. Note: A CoE is no longer valid if it is cancelled or the course is complete.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): You must
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), You must: A substantive visa ceases to be in effect if another substantive visa is granted. Applications are received Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST) (or Australian Eastern daylight standard time (AEDST) when applicable). Help with your visa. If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be a certain age (school student)
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be a certain age (school student): If you are a school student (but not participating in a secondary school student exchange program), you must be aged 6 or older to apply for this visa. You must also be: less than 17 years old when you begin Year 9. less than 18 years old when you begin Year 10. less than 19 years old when you begin Year 11. less than 20 years old when you begin Year 12.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence: You must include the right evidence of enrolment in study with your Student visa application, or your application will not be valid and can't be processed. Providing a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE). You must be enrolled in a full time course registered on the Commonwealth Register of Institutions and courses for Overseas Students (CRICOS). You must provide a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) for all intended courses when you apply. If you do not provide a CoE at time of lodgement, the student visa application will be invalid. Your CoE must be valid when we decide your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence: A CoE is no longer valid if it is cancelled or the course is complete. If you finish your course, but still require a student visa, you will need to attach a new CoE to your ImmiAccount. You must maintain enrolment in a course of study to be eligible for a student visa. Packaged courses and CoEs. If you are applying for more than one (1) course in your Student visa application, you must include all CoE codes in the application form, as your visa period may only consider the duration of the course according to the CoE provided.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence: You can apply to include two (2) or more courses on your Student visa where one course clearly leads to the next. Course gaps must be less than two calendar months, unless the first course finishes at the end of the standard academic year and the next course commences at the beginning of the standard academic year. If you want your Student visa to cover more than one (1) course you must include all CoE codes in your visa application form, or your visa may only cover the CoE provided.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence: If you are a student visa holder and you meet an exemption to lodge a further Student visa in Australia, you cannot package courses together unless you are applying for: primary or secondary school studies, or. a PHD degree, or. a further visa because your education provider defaulted. In all other scenarios, you can only apply in Australia for one further course. Other evidence of enrolment.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence: You do not need to provide a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) if you are: enrolled in a full-time course of study or training under a scholarship scheme approved by the Australian Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade: provide a letter of support. sponsored by the Australian Department of Defence: provide a letter of support. a secondary exchange student: provide an Acceptance Advice of Secondary Exchange Student (AASES) form. a postgraduate research student who needs to stay in Australia while your thesis is marked: provide a letter from your education provider.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Make Welfare arrangements if you are under 18 years
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Make Welfare arrangements if you are under 18 years: If you are applying for a Student visa and you are under 18 years of age, you must have adequate welfare arrangements in place while you are in Australia. If you will be 18 years of age when you arrive in Australia, you must tell us as you might not need to provide some of this information. To learn more, see Welfare arrangements for students under 18.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet English language requirements
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet English language requirements: You might need to provide evidence of your English language skills when you submit your visa application. If you need to provide evidence of your English language skills, you must prove that you: have obtained a certain test score in an English language test that the Department has approved, or. fall into an exemption category listed below. For more information on the minimum overall band scores you must achieve to meet the Student visa English language requirements, go to Gather Documents in the 'Step by Step' tab.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet English language requirements
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet English language requirements: To find out if you need to provide evidence of your English language skills when you apply, use the Document Checklist tool.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language tests
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language tests: You must have completed the English language test: within the 2 years before you lodged your visa application, if you are Regular Evidence level; or. within the 2 years before a decision is made on your visa application, if you are Streamlined Evidence level and the Department has requested evidence. At-home or online English language tests. The Department of Home Affairs does not accept evidence from English language tests where an entire test is delivered online (also known as “remote-proctored” or “at-home”).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language tests
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language tests: Examples of online tests that are not approved for Australian visa purposes, include: IELTS Online. LANGUAGECERT Academic Online. OET@Home. CELPIP Online. MET Digital (taken at-home). TOEFL iBT – Home Edition. TOEFL iBT. From 21 January 2026, applicants must select 'Taking TOEFL for Australia ’ during registration to ensure the test is valid for Australian visa purposes. We will not accept TOEFL iBT tests completed between 26 July 2023, and 4 May 2024 for Australian visa and migration purposes. During this period, the TOEFL iBT test being offered was not an approved test.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language tests
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language tests: Cambridge C1 Advanced test (previously known as Cambridge English: Advanced CAE). From 12 February 2024 to 6 August 2025, the department will only accept results from the Cambridge C1 Advanced paper-based test. The department will still accept tests taken before 12 February 2024 and within specified validity periods, for C1 Advanced paper-based and computer-based tests. LANGUAGECERT Academic. If you sit a LANGUAGECERT test, you will receive a ‘certificate’ and a ‘report’.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language tests
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language tests: If you use your LANGUAGECERT Academic results to show you meet the English language requirement, you must include both documents with your visa application. If you do not provide the certificate and the report, visa processing may be delayed.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language evidence exemptions
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language evidence exemptions: You do not need to give us evidence of an English test score with your visa application if one of the following applies: you are a citizen and hold a passport from UK, USA, Canada, NZ or Republic of Ireland. you are an applicant who is a Foreign Affairs or Defence sponsored student, or a Secondary Exchange student (AASES). you are enrolled in a principal course of study that is a registered school course. you are enrolled in a principal course of study that is a standalone English Language Intensive Course for Overseas Students (ELICOS). you are enrolled in a principal course of study registered and delivered in a language other than English. you are enrolled in a registered post-graduate research course. you have completed at least 5 years’ study in English in Australia, UK, USA, Canada, New Zealand, South Africa, or the Republic of Ireland. in the 2 years before applying for the Student visa you completed the Senior Secondary Certificate of Education in Australia in English while you held a Student visa. in the 2 years before applying for the Student visa you completed a substantial component of a course that would qualify you under the Australian Qualifications Framework at the Certificate IV or higher level, while you held a Student visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language evidence exemptions
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language evidence exemptions: Note: We may need you to give us evidence of an English test score with your visa application if you hold a British National Overseas (BNO) passport. If you are required to provide evidence of English language proficiency but you fall into an exemption category, make sure you provide the appropriate evidence that demonstrates that you satisfy one of the exemptions. For more information on English Language Tests and Evidence Exemptions refer to the Migration (English Language Tests and Evidence Exemptions for Subclass 500 (Student) Visas) Instrument 2025 - Federal Register of Legislation.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have adequate health insurance
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have adequate health insurance: You and your family members must have and maintain adequate health insurance for the whole of your stay in Australia. To find out the length of coverage you will require, see Student visa grant periods. You and your family members must be covered by Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) from an approved Australian health insurance provider, unless an 'Exception' applies. Applicants outside Australia. Your cover must start from the day you and your family arrive in Australia, not the day your course starts.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have adequate health insurance
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have adequate health insurance: If you have been granted a visa and want to travel to Australia before your course begins, the OSHC start date must be the same as the date you arrive, not the date your course starts. Generally this is a minimum of 1 week to 1 month before your course starts. You must: ensure you don't enter Australia before your OSHC begins, and. maintain your OSHC until you leave Australia. You may be refused entry to Australia if you cannot prove you have health insurance in place when you arrive. Applicants in Australia. Applicants must have OSHC.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have adequate health insurance
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have adequate health insurance: If your previous visa required you to have health insurance, cover must be continuous with no gap between your previous health cover and your OSHC. Exceptions. You do not need to have OSHC if you are: a Norwegian student covered by the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme. a Swedish student covered by Kammarkollegiet. a Belgian student covered under the Reciprocal Health Care Agreement with Australia. How to get Overseas Student Health Cover. To get OSHC: find an approved provider. pay for your policy. Your education provider or agent might arrange OSHC for you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have adequate health insurance
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have adequate health insurance: If your education provider arranges your OSHC coverage, you will need to know the name of your health insurance provider, the date that your policy starts and finishes and should be aware of the terms and conditions of your policy. Your education provider will also need to include your health insurance information on your Certificate of Enrolment (CoE). If you arrange OSHC coverage yourself, you will need to know the policy number to include in the visa application. We will refuse your visa application if you don't give us this information when you apply for your Student visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have adequate health insurance
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have adequate health insurance: Insurance for family members. If you have a single OSHC policy and you have family members, including children born in Australia after your arrival, consider getting a family policy. Every member of your family must have health insurance. Any family member who joins you after you arrive in Australia must show us they have OSHC for the duration of their stay in Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Apply from the right location
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Apply from the right location: From 2 October 2026, new rules mean that most Student visa applications must be lodged outside Australia. You can only apply in Australia if you hold an eligible visa and meet an exemption category. Eligible visas. If you hold a visa as a primary or secondary holder on the list below you cannot apply for a student visa in Australia. There are no exemptions to this rule. Subclass 400 – Temporary Work (all streams). Subclass 403 – (Domestic Worker – Diplomatic/Consular stream). Subclass 407 – Training (all streams). Subclass 408 – Temporary Activity (all streams).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Apply from the right location
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Apply from the right location: Subclass 417 – Working Holiday (all streams). Subclass 457 – Temporary Work (all streams). Subclass 462 – Work and Holiday (all streams). Subclass 482 – Skills in Demand / Temporary Skill Shortage (all streams). Subclass 485 – Temporary Graduate. Subclass 600 – Visitor. Subclass 601 – ETA. Subclass 602 – Medical Treatment. Subclass 651 – eVisitor. Subclass 771 – Transit. Subclass 988 – Maritime Crew. Subclass 995 – Diplomatic (Temporary) (primary only. A family member of a Diplomatic (Temporary) visa (subclass 995) can apply for a Student visa in Australia).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet an exemption to apply for a further student visa in Australia
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet an exemption to apply for a further student visa in Australia: If you are student visa holder you may be able to apply for another Student visa while in Australia. Dependent or secondary student visa holders cannot apply for a student visa as the primary applicant while in Australia. If you hold a student visa as the primary applicant, you may be able to apply in Australia if you meet one of the six exemptions below. If you do not meet an exemption, you should not apply in Australia. We will not accept your application if you are not eligible and this may have consequences if you are in Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet an exemption to apply for a further student visa in Australia
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet an exemption to apply for a further student visa in Australia: An invalid application outcome could affect your visa status and you may not be eligible to apply for a further visa if your visa has already expired. Invalid decisions cannot be merits reviewed at the ART.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 1 – you need up to 12 additional months to complete your studies (course completion).
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 1 – you need up to 12 additional months to complete your studies (course completion).: To apply under this exemption: you need up to 12 additional months from the original end date of your main course to finish your course, and. the course you are completing must be the main course in your package of courses (if you are studying packaged courses), and. the course must be with the same education provider that your current Student visa was granted for (you can have changed courses but the course you changed to must be at the same AQF level or higher).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 1 – you need up to 12 additional months to complete your studies (course completion).
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 1 – you need up to 12 additional months to complete your studies (course completion).: For example, students who have started a Bachelor’s Degree can apply for a student visa in Australia if they need up to 12 extra months to finish the same degree or a different Bachelor degree at the same education provider. If you do not meet this exemption criteria you will need to lodge your next application from outside Australia. To help minimise your time outside Australia and any interruptions to your studies, make sure you prepare your application and supporting documents before leaving Australia. For more information about applying from outside Australia, see the Student visa changes.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 1 – you need up to 12 additional months to complete your studies (course completion).
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 1 – you need up to 12 additional months to complete your studies (course completion).: Understanding AQF levels and VET courses. The Australian qualifications are ranked from level 1 to level 10 by the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF). Check the AQF level of your current and proposed course to see whether you meet the course completion exemption.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 2 – you are sponsored by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) or Defence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 2 – you are sponsored by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) or Defence: To apply under this exemption, you must be sponsored by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade or the Department of Defence.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 3 – you are applying to undertake a PhD Degree
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 3 – you are applying to undertake a PhD Degree: To apply under this exemption, you must be applying to study a Doctoral Degree (PhD). You cannot apply under this exemption if you are applying to study a Master’s by Research course.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 4 – you are applying to undertake primary or secondary school studies
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 4 – you are applying to undertake primary or secondary school studies: To apply under this exemption, you must be applying to study primary or secondary school studies.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression)
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression): To apply under this exemption: you must have completed your main course for which your visa was granted for or you have completed a course which was the same or higher AQF level as the original course your student visa was granted for, and. you are progressing to a course at a higher AQF level, and. if your completed course was a higher education course, the course you are progressing to must also be a higher education course delivered by a higher education provider.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression)
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression): You can also apply for this exemption: if the main course you completed did not have an AQF level, and you are progressing to a course with an AQF level or. you have completed your school studies and are progressing to a course that does not have an AQF level. For example: Students who have completed an English Language Intensive Courses for Overseas Students (ELICOS) course can apply for a student visa in Australia if they are progressing to a Bachelor’s Degree.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression)
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression): Students who have completed an ELICOS course cannot apply for a student visa in Australia if they want to study another ELICOS course. Students who have completed their secondary school studies can apply for a student visa in Australia if they want to study a foundational course after they finish school. Students who have completed a Bachelor’s Degree at a higher education provider cannot apply for a student visa in Australia if they want to study a Graduate Diploma course at a VET provider. Packaged courses.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression)
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression): If you are applying under the course progression exemption you: cannot package courses. must be enrolled in only one future course of study when you apply. If you are enrolled in more than one future course, you may not meet the requirements for a valid application. You are expected to begin your next course in the first available intake after completing your current course. The gap between courses should be minimal and, in most cases, no longer than two calendar months during the teaching year or four calendar months between standard academic years.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression)
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression): For example if you: are a Year 12 student relying on the course progression exemption, you cannot apply in Australia for a package that includes a Foundation course followed by a Bachelor degree. You will need to apply outside Australia. have finished a Bachelor Degree and you are applying to undertake a Graduate Certificate and a Master’s Degree, you will need to apply outside Australia. If you meet the course progression exemption, when you submit your visa application, you must provide evidence that you have completed your course.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression)
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course (course progression): You must attach documents such as: your academic transcripts. a course completion certificate. a letter from your education provider confirming you have completed your course. Understanding AQF levels and VET courses. The Australian qualifications are ranked from level 1 to level 10 by the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF). Check the AQF level of your current and proposed course to see whether you meet the course progression exemption.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 6 – you cannot continue your course because your education provider has defaulted
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 6 – you cannot continue your course because your education provider has defaulted: To apply under this exemption, you must be unable to continue your course because your education provider has defaulted. For more information, see Education provider default.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet an exemption if you want to include family members
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet an exemption if you want to include family members: If you meet one of the exemptions below, your family members must apply at the same time and from the same location as you. If your family members are applying with you in Australia, they must hold an eligible visa to apply. If you do not meet an exemption to include family, you should not lodge an application for your family members. We will not accept your family member’s application if they are not eligible and this may have consequences if they are in Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet an exemption if you want to include family members
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet an exemption if you want to include family members: An invalid application outcome could affect their visa status and they may not be eligible to apply for a further visa if their visa has already expired. Invalid decisions cannot be merits reviewed at the ART.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 1 – you are a Doctoral (PhD) student
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 1 – you are a Doctoral (PhD) student: To include family under this exemption, you must be applying to study a Doctoral Degree (PhD). You cannot apply under this exemption if you are applying to study a Master’s by Research course. You can include family members when you lodge your visa application inside or outside Australia. If your family members are applying in Australia, they must hold an eligible visa or a student visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 2 – you are a Department of Defence or Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade sponsored student
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 2 – you are a Department of Defence or Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade sponsored student: To include family under this exemption, you must be sponsored by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade or the Department of Defence. You can include family members when you lodge your visa application inside or outside Australia. If your family members are applying in Australia, they must hold an eligible visa or a student visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 3 – you are a foreign government scholarship recipient
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 3 – you are a foreign government scholarship recipient: To include family under this exemption, you must be receiving a foreign government scholarship that fully funds your studies in Australia. If you are outside Australia, you can include family members when you lodge your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 3 – you are a foreign government scholarship recipient
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 3 – you are a foreign government scholarship recipient: If you are inside Australia, you can only include family members when you lodge your application if you: need up to 12 additional months to complete the main course covered by your current Student visa, or. have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course at a higher Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) level. if your completed course was a higher education course, the course you are progressing to must also be a higher education course delivered by a higher education provider, or. need to lodge a further Student visa application because your education provider defaulted.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries: To include family under this exemption, you must be a national from a Pacific Island: Federated States of Micronesia. Kiribati. Papua New Guinea. Republic of the Marshall Islands. Solomon Islands. Vanuatu. Or an ASEAN country: Brunei Darussalam. Cambodia. Indonesia. Lao Peoples Dem Republic. Malaysia. Myanmar. Philippines. Singapore. Thailand. Timor-Leste. Vietnam. If you are outside Australia, you can include family members when you lodge your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries: If you are inside Australia, you can only include family members when you lodge your application if you: need up to 12 additional months to complete the main course covered by your current Student visa, or. have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course at a higher Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) level.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries: If your completed course was a higher education course, the course you are progressing to must also be a higher education course delivered by a higher education provider, or. need to lodge a further Student visa application because your education provider defaulted.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – Other exemptions
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – Other exemptions: Current Student visa holders applying inside or outside Australia. If you currently hold a Student visa and you are inside or outside Australia, you can include family members who are currently on your Student visa when you lodge your application, if: you need up to 12 additional months to complete your main course covered by your current Student visa, or. you need to lodge a further Student visa application because your education provider defaulted. Current student visa holders applying inside Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – Other exemptions
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – Other exemptions: If you currently hold a student visa and you are inside Australia, you can include family members who are currently on your student visa when you lodge your application, if: you have completed your main course for which your student visa was granted for or you have completed a course which was the same or higher AQF level as the original course your student visa was granted for, and. you are progressing to a course at a higher AQF level, and. if your completed course was a higher education course, the course you are progressing to must also be a higher education course delivered by a higher education provider.

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Maintain Enrolment
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Maintain Enrolment: If you provided a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) with your application as evidence of enrolment in study, you must hold a valid CoE when we decide your student visa application. attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Biometrics
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Biometrics: We might ask for biometrics. Most applicants will be advised immediately after submitting an application if you need to provide biometrics. You will receive a letter and will also be able to see this request in your ImmiAccount. You will be given 14 days to provide biometrics so it is important to arrange an appointment quickly using the instructions in the request letter. You must provide biometrics before travelling to Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Health exams

attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Stay lawful in Australia
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Stay lawful in Australia: Make sure you stay lawful by holding a valid visa while we process your application. If you were in Australia when you applied for this visa, you were granted a Bridging visa A (BVA). If your current visa expires before we decide on your application, the BVA will start. You can stay in Australia on the BVA while we process your new visa application. You cannot travel on the BVA - there is no right of return on this visa; it cancels on departure. Do not cancel your current visa. If you do, you will: be staying in Australia unlawfully. not be eligible for a Bridging visa A.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

If you lodged your application from outside Australia, because you were not eligible to lodge your application in Australia, you may travel to Australia on another valid visa while your Student visa application is being processed. You must comply with that visa’s conditions. If you applied from outside Australia, because you were not eligible to lodge your application in Australia, you must be outside Australia when the Student visa is granted.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Travel after you apply

You will not receive a Bridging visa linked to an application lodged outside Australia. You applied outside Australia, but you are eligible to lodge inside Australia. If you lodged your application from outside Australia, but you are eligible under an exemption to lodge your application inside Australia, you can be granted your student visa while you are in Australia. For more information, see Exemptions – for student visa holders.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

If you lodged your application in Australia, you do not have to tell us if you want to travel outside Australia while we process your application. This is because you can be outside Australia when we make a decision. But if you leave Australia, make sure your visa allows you to return. If you have a Bridging visa A, it will cease if you leave Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Travel after you apply

If you can’t provide a birth certificate, provide one of the following: identification pages of a family book showing the names of both parents. identification pages of an identification document issued by the government. identification pages of a court-issued document that proves your identity. identification pages of a family census register.

Anyone with a legal right to decide where you live, and who is not travelling in Australia with you, must complete either: Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years. a statutory declaration giving their consent for you to visit Australia on this visa.

This could include: proof you have enough money for your stay and to leave Australia, such as personal bank statements, pay slips, audited accounts, tax records or credit card limit. a letter from your relative or friend in Australia, inviting you to visit. The letter could state: their relationship to you. the purpose of your visit and length of stay. if you will be staying with them. If this person will be paying for your stay, provide proof of their funds. your plans while in Australia.

This can include: birth certificates. passport pages showing names of parents. family register. marriage certificates. Example. If your aunt is sponsoring you, you need to attach a document or a set of documents, which collectively prove the relationship.

abstract: Visitor visa (subclass 600), Sponsored Family stream, Group applications: Some visa applications allow two or more applicants travelling together as a group to have their separate applications processed together. Applicants may create a group on the ‘Manage groups’ tab in ImmiAccount. Applications that allow for group processing will ask about this on the second page. Applicants should be aware that generally, we will process the applications together. We process each application in the group on its own merits. Apply online.

title: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601): Have an eligible passport
abstract: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601), Have an eligible passport: You must hold a valid passport from one of these countries or jurisdictions to be eligible for an ETA. You cannot apply for an ETA with a non-citizen passport, certificate of identity or other travel document, such as a Titre de Voyage. Andorra. Austria. Belgium. Denmark. Finland. Germany. Hong Kong (SAR of China). Iceland. Ireland. Liechtenstein. Luxembourg. Malaysia. Portugal. Republic of San Marino. Singapore. South Korea. Switzerland. Taiwan (excluding official or diplomatic passports). The Netherlands. United Kingdom—British Citizen. United Kingdom—British National (Overseas).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601): Have an eligible passport
abstract: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601), Have an eligible passport: United States of America. Vatican City. If you hold more than one passport, you must declare this in your ETA application and provide details of your other passports. If you hold an ETA eligible passport, but you are also an Australian citizen, you cannot apply for an ETA. Australian citizens have an automatic right of entry and do not need a visa to enter Australia. See Travelling as a dual citizen.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

If you will be entering health care or hospital environments, you should apply for a Visitor (subclass 600) visa.

If you are granted an ETA, but we find that you provided incorrect information, your ETA may be cancelled.

title: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601): Before you apply
abstract: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601), Before you apply: Check you have a valid passport. Download the Australian ETA app for free from the Apple Store (Apple) or Google Play Store (Android). Watch the ETA and AIA video guides. Help with your application. Travel industry representatives can use the Australian ETA app to help you apply. They must take a live facial image of you when they lodge the application. We will not grant you a visa if you do not take a live image. More information for industry representatives is available at: Australian ETA app - Guidance notes for industry users (English).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601): Apply using the Australian ETA app
abstract: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601), Apply using the Australian ETA app: To apply for an ETA using the Australian ETA app, you need to have: A mobile device with a camera which can take your photo and an image of the Passport data page. Near-field communication (NFC) enabled on your mobile device. Location services enabled on your mobile device. A valid email address. A valid payment method ready to pay the service fee. You can't include family members in your application. Each family member, including those listed on your passport, must submit a separate application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601): Apply using the Australian ETA app
abstract: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601), Apply using the Australian ETA app: If all family members apply using the same mobile device, you can submit and pay for the applications at the same time. You can get help from a friend or family member to apply through the app but you must be physically with them when you apply. Authorised travel agents and industry representatives can also make an ETA application on your behalf using the app. More information for industry representatives is available at: Australian ETA app - Guidance notes for industry users (English). Australian ETA app - Guidance notes for industry users (Japanese).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601): Apply using the Australian ETA app
abstract: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601), Apply using the Australian ETA app: Australian ETA app - Guidance notes for industry users (Korean). If an agent applies on your behalf, you must still be physically present when they make the application. You will need to take your photo and have your passport available to scan.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601): Apply using the Australian ETA app
abstract: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601), Apply using the Australian ETA app: After you have downloaded and opened the app on your mobile device, you need to: scan your passport to pre-fill your name, date of birth, passport number and other details. take a photo of yourself. answer some questions, including whether you have any criminal convictions, any prior names and contact details in Australia. pay the service fee. submit the application. Republic of Cyprus. Denmark. Estonia. Finland. Germany. Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China. Republic of Ireland. Republic of Korea. Netherlands. Taiwan, other than an official or diplomatic passport. The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland (including British National Overseas passport holders).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Current or previous visa
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Current or previous visa: You must: hold or previously have held one Working Holiday visa (subclass 417). if in Australia, hold a substantive visa or your last substantive visa expired less than 28 days ago. have entered Australia on the visa. have complied with all the conditions on your first Working Holiday visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Have enough money
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Have enough money: You must have enough money to: support yourself while you are in Australia. leave Australia at the end of your stay. This is usually about AUD5,000 for your initial stay plus the fare to where you are going when you leave Australia. If you are applying in Australia, you don’t need to provide evidence. If you are applying outside Australia and don’t attach evidence to your application, processing may be delayed if we need to contact you to request further information.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Specified work
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Specified work: You must have completed 3 months of specified subclass 417 work. UK passport holders can be granted a second Working Holiday (subclass 417) visa without having to meet the 3 months of specified subclass 417 work if they apply on or after 1 July 2024 using their UK passport. For more information, see New arrangements for UK passport holders.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Be this age
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Be this age: At the time of application, you must be within the eligible age limit for your passport country: Belgium – 18 to 30 years. Canada – 18 to 35 years. Republic of Cyprus - 18 to 35 years. Denmark - 18 to 35 years. Estonia - 18 to 30 years. Finland - 18 to 35 years. France - 18 to 35 years. Germany - 18 to 35 years. Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China - 18 to 30 years. Republic of Ireland - 18 to 35 years. Italy - 18 to 35 years. Japan - 18 to 30 years. Republic of Korea - 18 to 35 years. Malta - 18 to 30 years. Netherlands - 18 to 30 years.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Be this age
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Be this age: Norway - 18 to 30 years. Sweden - 18 to 30 years. Taiwan (other than an official or diplomatic passport) - 18 to 30 years. The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland - 18 to 35 years (including British National Overseas passport holders. ** You must apply for your visa before you turn 31 (or 36) years old in Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST)/Australian Eastern Daylight Savings Time (AEDST). The deadline to lodge an application is midnight AEST/AEDST the day before your 31st or 36th birthday. This time applies even if you are applying from outside Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Be this age
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Be this age: Note that AEST/AEDST will be different to when your birthday ends in your country due to time differences between countries. *** Avoid submitting your application on your birthday, if possible. We can still grant you the visa if you apply for it at 30 (or 35) but turn 31 (or 36) years old before we make a decision. You must still meet all other requirements.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Meet the health requirement
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Meet the health requirement: You must meet our health requirement.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Meet the character requirement
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Meet the character requirement: You must meet our character requirement.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Pay your debts to the Australian Government
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Pay your debts to the Australian Government: If you or any family members (including those who don't apply for the visa with you) owe the Australian government money, you or they must have paid it back or arranged to pay it back.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Not had a visa cancelled or an application refused
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Not had a visa cancelled or an application refused: We will consider your immigration history when we make a decision on your application, which means you might not be eligible for this visa if you have had a visa cancelled or refused. In some circumstances you may still apply for a permanent visa if you have had a visa cancelled or an application refused see Limitations on applications in Australia. If applying for a visa from outside Australia see Can I go to Australia. If you want immigration assistance, see Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Sign the Australian values statement
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Sign the Australian values statement: You must acknowledge the Australian Values Statement that confirms you will respect the Australian way of life and obey Australian laws when you apply for the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Organise health exams: You might need to have health examinations. You can complete them before you apply or you can wait and have them if we tell you to. Find out the examinations you need and how to arrange them if you want to have them before you apply.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Get help with your application
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Get help with your application: Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be: a registered migration agent. a legal practitioner, or. an exempt person. You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Gather your documents: Provide accurate information. See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Identity documents
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Identity documents: Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates. Also provide a copy of your birth certificate showing both your parents’ names. If you don’t have a birth certificate and you can’t get one, provide a copy of the identification pages of one of these: a family book showing both your parents’ names. government-issued identification. a court-issued document that verifies your identity.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Identity documents
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Identity documents: If you have changed your name, provide proof such as: a marriage or divorce certificate. change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority. documents that show other names you have been known by.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Enough money for your stay and to leave
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Enough money for your stay and to leave: Provide evidence you have enough money for your stay in Australia. This is usually AUD5,000. You must also show us you have enough money to buy a ticket to leave Australia at the end of your stay, or that you already have the ticket. If you are applying in Australia, you don’t need to provide evidence. If you are applying outside Australia and don’t attach evidence to your application, processing may be delayed if we need to contact you to request further information.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Proof of specified subclass 417 work
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Proof of specified subclass 417 work: Provide proof that you have completed 3 months of specified subclass 417 work on your previous WHM visa (or in other eligible circumstances). The proof must cover all periods you worked. You can include any of the following: pay slips. Australian bank statements covering the period of declared specified work. piece rate agreement with your employer, if you were paid piece rates. The agreement must show the pay rate per piece and how it is measured. group certificates. payment summaries. tax returns. employer references. a written and signed agreement setting out any lawful deductions in pay.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Proof of specified subclass 417 work
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Proof of specified subclass 417 work: Note: We might contact your employer(s) to check your work claims. If you have completed volunteer bushfire or flood recovery work, provide: a signed letter from your volunteer coordinator or host including: your personal details including passport number. description of volunteer duties undertaken. location of volunteer work including postcode(s). number of days you provided volunteer assistance.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Character documents
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Character documents: We might ask you to provide: an Australian police certificate if you have spent a total of 12 months or more in Australia in the last 10 years since you turned 16. We only accept complete disclosure National Police Certificates issued by the Australian Federal Police.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Character documents
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Character documents: We do not accept standard disclosure certificates or national police certificates issued by Australian state or territory police. an overseas police certificate from every country, including your home country, where you spent a total of 12 months or more in the last 10 years since you turned 16. military service records or discharge papers if you served in the armed forces of any country. We will let you know if you need to give us these documents.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Tell us you are getting help
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Tell us you are getting help: To nominate someone to: receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person. Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Translate
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Translate: Have all non-English documents translated into English. Provide original and translated documents in your application. Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters. Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their: full name. address and telephone number. qualifications and experience in the language they are translating. These details must be in English. Note: You do not need to have any documents certified.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Scan or photograph
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Scan or photograph: Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour. The scans and photos must be clear. If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Attach
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Attach: Attach a document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing. Learn more about attaching documents.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Provide accurate information

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Apply online
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Apply online: Log in or create an ImmiAccount. Attach documents. Pay the application fee. We will not process your application until you pay the fee. Note the Transaction reference number. Applicants with dependent children. You can’t apply online if you are the parent of a child under the age of 18. Working Holiday visa holders cannot be accompanied by dependent children at any time during their stay in Australia. While it is possible to obtain a Working Holiday visa if you have a child, your child cannot join you in Australia at any time while you are on your Working Holiday visa – not even for one day.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: After you apply
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, After you apply: See what you can and must do after you apply. We will let you know when we have received your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: You applied in Australia
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, You applied in Australia: Tell us if you want to travel outside Australia while we process your application. We need to know because you must be in Australia when we decide your application. If you leave Australia, make sure you have a valid visa to return. You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is valid. Time spent outside Australia does not extend the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: You applied outside Australia
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, You applied outside Australia: Do not arrange to travel to Australia until we let you know, in writing, that we have granted you the visa.

attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Tell us if things change
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Tell us if things change: Tell us if things change after you lodge your application but before we decide your visa. If we grant your visa, we will tell you: your visa grant number. the date your visa starts. your visa conditions. Keep a copy of the decision notification with you when in Australia. If we refuse your visa, we will tell you: why we refused the visa. if you have a right to a review of the decision.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), third Working Holiday visa, You must: have previously held 2 subclass 417 visas in Australia. You can’t include family members in your application. Help with your visa.
