abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, What will happen after you apply: We will let you know when we have received your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Status updates
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Status updates: We can’t give updates on applications within the standard processing time. Wait for us to contact you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Travel after you apply
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Travel after you apply: If you are in Australia, you don't have to tell us if you want to travel outside Australia while we process your application. This is because you can be outside Australia when we decide on your application. But if you leave Australia, make sure you have a valid visa to return. Learn about visa expiry. Learn about Bridging visas.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Health exams
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Health exams: If you didn't have health examinations before you applied, we will let you know if you need them. Check ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Biometrics
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Biometrics: We might ask for biometrics (fingerprints and photo). We will let you know if you need to provide them.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Attach more information
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Attach more information: We might ask you to provide more information. Attach any additional documents we ask you for as soon as possible in ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Stay lawful
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Stay lawful: Make sure you stay lawful by holding a valid visa while we process your application. When you apply for this visa in Australia, you are likely to be granted a bridging visa. If your current visa expires before we decide your application, the bridging visa will start. You can stay in Australia on the bridging visa while we process your new visa application. Learn more about visa expiry.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Pay the second instalment
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Pay the second instalment: If you need to pay a second instalment, we will send you an invoice after you have met all other requirements for the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Add family
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Add family: You can add family members to your application before we decide on your visa. For the purpose of adding family members to this visa, your family members are: your partner. your dependent child and stepchild. your partner's dependent child and stepchild.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Newborn children
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Newborn children: Find out what to do if you had a baby.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Mistakes on your application
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Mistakes on your application: Let us know as soon as you can if you made a mistake on your application. Complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Help with your application
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Help with your application: Let us know if you no longer want someone to: receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person. Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount. For more information see Who can help you with your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Tell us if things change
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Tell us if things change: Tell us if things change after you submit your application but before we decide on your application. Things you need to let us know about include: you want to withdraw your application. changes to your phone number, address or passport. changes to your relationship status. the birth of a child. See what to do if your situation changes.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Additional information for after you apply
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Additional information for after you apply: We might ask you to get a skills assessment.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Visa outcome
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Visa outcome: New step description.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream: Visa outcome
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Temporary Residence Transition stream, Visa outcome: You can be inside or outside Australia when we decide on your application. If we grant your visa, we will tell you: your visa grant number. the date your visa starts. your visa conditions, if applicable. Keep a copy of the decision. If we refuse your visa, we will tell you: why we refused the visa. whether you have a right to a review of the decision. We will not refund the visa application charge if we refuse your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: With this visa you can
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, With this visa you can: live, work and study in Australia indefinitely. sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia. apply for Australian citizenship, if eligible.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: How long you can stay
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, How long you can stay: Permanently.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Cost
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Cost: Concessions apply in limited circumstances. Cost Concession. From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application. See About this visa. To see what your visa will cost use the Visa Pricing Estimator. The estimator does not consider the second instalment or other costs.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: You must
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, You must: be under 45 years old on the date you lodge your application, unless exempt. be nominated for an occupation on the Core Skills Occupation List. have at least 3 years relevant work experience, unless you are exempt. have a positive skills assessment before you lodge your application, unless you are exempt. meet minimum standards of English language proficiency. meet health and character requirements. Help with your visa. If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help you with your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Have an eligible occupation
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Have an eligible occupation: Your occupation must be on the Core Skills Occupation List (CSOL).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Have relevant work experience
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Have relevant work experience: Unless exempt, most applicants need to have at least 3 years relevant work experience in their occupation. Applicants who are exempt from the skills assessment requirement are also exempt from the work experience requirement.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Licensing, registration or membership
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Licensing, registration or membership: You must be licensed, registered or a member of a professional body if it is mandatory in the state or territory you intend to work in.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Have a positive skills assessment
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Have a positive skills assessment: Most applicants need to have a skills assessment that shows they have the skills to work in the nominated position. Learn more about skills assessments.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Exemption
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Exemption: You are exempt from having a skills assessment if you: have been nominated as an academic (university lecturer or faculty head at Academic Level A, B, C, D or E) by a university in Australia, or. have been nominated as a scientist, researcher or technical specialist by an Australian government scientific agency, or. currently hold a Special Category (subclass 444) or New Zealand Citizen Family Relationship (subclass 461) visa and have worked for the employer who nominated you, in the nominated position, for at least 2 years in the last 3 years prior to the date you applied for the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Be nominated
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Be nominated: You must be nominated by an Australian employer whose business is actively and lawfully operating. You must apply for the visa within 6 months of the nomination being approved. We can't grant you a visa if: we are aware of adverse information about your nominator or any person associated with them, unless it is reasonable to disregard this information, or. the nomination is withdrawn, or. the position is no longer available. You might be eligible for a refund of the visa application charge depending on the circumstances.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Be this age
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Be this age: Usually, you must be under 45 years of age when you apply.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Be this age
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Be this age: You are exempt from this criteria if any of the following applies to you: you are nominated as an academic (university lecturer or faculty head at Academic Level B, C D or E) by a university in Australia. you are nominated as a scientist, researcher or technical (scientific) specialist at ANZSCO skill level 1 or 2 by a Federal, State or Territory government science agency, or an Australian university. you currently hold a Special Category (subclass 444) or New Zealand citizen's family member (subclass 461) visa and have worked for the employer who nominated you, in the nominated position, for at least 2 years in the last 3 years immediately before you apply.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Be this age
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Be this age: The 2 years excludes periods of unpaid leave.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Meet our health requirement
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Meet our health requirement: You and any family members who apply for the visa with you must meet our health requirement. We might ask for health information about family not coming to Australia with you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Meet our character requirement
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Meet our character requirement: You and family members aged 16 years and over who apply for the visa with you must meet our character requirement. We might ask for character information about family not coming to Australia with you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Sign the Australian values statement
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Sign the Australian values statement: If you are 18 years of age or older, you must: have read, or had explained to you, the Life in Australia booklet and. sign an Australian Values Statement that confirms you will respect the Australian way of life and obey Australian laws.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Have this level of English language
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Have this level of English language: You must have at least competent English to be granted this stream of the visa. Any dependent applicant who was aged at least 18 years on the day you make your application should provide evidence they have at least functional English. If you can't show that they have functional English, you will need to pay the second instalment of the visa application charge when we ask you to.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Have paid back your debt to the Australian government
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Have paid back your debt to the Australian government: If you owe the Australian Government money, you must have paid it back or have a formal arrangement to pay it back.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Not have had a visa cancelled or a previous application refused
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Not have had a visa cancelled or a previous application refused: We will consider your immigration history when we make a decision on your application, which means you might not be eligible for this visa if you have had a visa cancelled or refused. In some circumstances you may still apply for a permanent visa if you have had a visa cancelled or an application refused see Limitations on applications in Australia. If applying for a visa from outside Australia see Can I go to Australia. If you want immigration assistance, see Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Before you apply
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Before you apply: New step description.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Get your skills assessed
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Get your skills assessed: Get a skills assessment if you need to. The assessment will prove you have the right skills and qualifications to do your job. You must have received a positive outcome for your skills assessment before you apply for your visa. It cannot have been issued more than 3 years before the date you make your application. Occupations in the CSOL are benchmarked to the 2022 version of ANZSCO.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Get your skills assessed
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Get your skills assessed: Where occupation classifications have changed through ANZSCO updates, a skills assessment under the earlier ANZSCO classification will generally be accepted if: the skills assessment issued is still valid (up to three years, or less if the assessing authority specifies a shorter period),. the assessing authority was specified for the occupation at the time of the skills assessment, and. the nominated occupation corresponds to the historical classification of the occupation in ANZSCO. We do not accept skills assessments obtained for a subclass 485 visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Organise English exams
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Organise English exams: Make sure your English test results are current for this visa. Your English test results cannot have been issued more than three years before you make your application. You must also receive your test results before you lodge your visa application. Have English exams if necessary.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Get help with your application
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Get help with your application: Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be: a registered migration agent. a legal practitioner, or. an exempt person. You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Get the nomination Transaction Reference Number
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Get the nomination Transaction Reference Number: Make sure your employer has submitted a nomination application. They will receive a nomination Transaction Reference Number (TRN) when they do. Ask your employer for the TRN. You need it to apply for the visa. You do not need to wait for the nomination to be approved to lodge your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Your rights and your employer's obligations
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Your rights and your employer's obligations: Criminal and civil penalties can be applied to anyone who asks for, receives, offers or provides a benefit in exchange for visa sponsorship. Learn more about work visa scams.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Gather your documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Gather your documents: New step description.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Provide accurate information
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Provide accurate information: Provide accurate information. See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Identity documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Identity documents: Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates. If you have changed your name for any reason, you must also provide evidence of this. Documents that prove a change of name include: a marriage or divorce certificate. change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority. documents that show other names you have been known by.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Licencing, registration or membership
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Licencing, registration or membership: Provide evidence of any licence, registration or professional membership mandatory to perform the nominated occupation in the state or territory you intend to work in, if applicable. If you are a doctor, provide one of these certificates issued by the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency as proof of full registration: unconditional or general medical registration. conditional specialist registration which allows you to practise only in your particular specialty with no further training or supervision requirements.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Licencing, registration or membership
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Licencing, registration or membership: If you are a barrister or solicitor, provide proof of admission to practise as a lawyer in the relevant state or territory.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Skills and qualifications documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Skills and qualifications documents: Provide either: documents that prove your skills and qualifications. documents to prove you are exempt from proving your skills and qualifications.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Proof of your skills and qualifications
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Proof of your skills and qualifications: Provide all of the following: a positive and valid skills assessment, if required. your curriculum vitae (CV) or resume. qualifications and proof of work experience; such as employment references, if required.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Skills assessment exemption documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Skills assessment exemption documents: If you are exempt from having a skills assessment, provide proof that: you have been nominated as an academic (university lecturer or faculty head at Academic Level A, B, C, D or E) by a university in Australia, or. you are nominated as a scientist, researcher or technical (scientific) specialist at ANZSCO skill level 1 or 2 by a Federal, State or Territory government science agency, or an Australian university, or. you currently hold a Special Category (subclass 444) or New Zealand Citizen Family Relationship (subclass 461) visa and have worked for the employer who nominated you, in the nominated position, for at least 2 years in the last 3 years prior to the date you applied for the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Age exemption documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Age exemption documents: If you are 45 years old or older, provide documents to show you are exempt from the age eligibility criteria.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Age exemption documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Age exemption documents: You are exempt from this criteria if any of the following apply to you: you are nominated as an academic (university lecturer or faculty head at Academic Level B, C D or E) by a university in Australia. you are nominated as a scientist, researcher or technical (scientific) specialist at ANZSCO skill level 1 or 2 by a Federal, State or Territory government science agency, or an Australian university. you currently hold a Special Category (subclass 444) or New Zealand citizen's family member (subclass 461) visa and have worked for the employer who nominated you, in the nominated position, for at least 2 years in the last 3 years immediately before you apply.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Age exemption documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Age exemption documents: The 2 years excludes periods of unpaid leave.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, English language documents: Provide documents that show you have Competent English.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Health documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Health documents: You do not need to provide health documents. If you have had medical exams, the results are sent to us by your doctor.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Character documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Character documents: Provide an Australian police certificate if you have spent a total of 12 months or more in Australia in the last 10 years since you turned 16. We only accept complete disclosure National Police Certificates issued by the Australian Federal Police. We do not accept standard disclosure certificates or national police certificates issued by Australian state or territory police. For immigration purposes, Australian police certificates are valid for 12 months from the date of issue.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Character documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Character documents: Also provide: an overseas police certificate from every country, including your home country, where you have spent a total of 12 months or more in the last 10 years since you turned 16 if required, penal check letters are available by contacting espd@homeaffairs.gov.au and include the words “Front end load – Penal Check Letter” in the subject line of your email.. military service records or discharge papers if you served in the armed forces of any country. Further information is available at: Character requirements for visas.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Tell us you are getting help
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Tell us you are getting help: To nominate someone to: receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person. Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Partner documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Partner documents: Provide: identity documents. character documents. Provide either: your current marriage certificate or. enough documents to prove your partner has been in a de facto relationship with you for at least 12 months before you apply. Documents that prove a de facto relationship include: joint bank account statements. billing accounts in joint names. joint leases or mortgages. documents that show you have both lived at the same address.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Proof of Functional English
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Proof of Functional English: You must show that your family member over 18 has functional English. If you can't show that your family member has functional English, you will need to pay the second instalment when we ask you to.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Dependants under 18 documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Dependants under 18 documents: For every dependant under 18 years who is applying with you provide: identity documents (if your child is under 5 years old you can include them in the application without a passport). proof of their relationship with you such as a birth or marriage certificate. character documents, if applicable.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Parental responsibility documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Parental responsibility documents: You must get consent for the child to come to Australia from anyone who: has a legal right to decide where the child lives and. is not coming to Australia with the child. They must complete either: Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years. a statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to visit Australia on this visa. Include a document with the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, such as a: passport. driver’s licence.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Dependants over 18 documents: For every dependant 18 years old or older who is applying with you provide: identity documents. documents about other relationships, if applicable. character documents.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Proof of dependence
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Proof of dependence: You need to prove that this person is a family member and/or dependent on you. Provide: a completed Form 47a Details of a child or other dependent family member aged 18 years or over. proof of your relationship with the dependent such as a birth certificate or adoption papers. You must also prove this person has been financially dependent on you for at least 12 months before you apply. You could provide: proof they live with you. their tax records. proof they are currently studying.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Proof of dependence
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Proof of dependence: For other family members, if applicable, provide evidence the person: holds a subclass 457 or subclass 482 visa. was granted that visa because they were your family member and. is included in your application for this subclass 186 visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Proof of Functional English
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Proof of Functional English: You must show that your family member has functional English. If you can't show that your family member has functional English, you will need to pay the second instalment when we ask you to.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Translate
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Translate: Have all non-English documents translated into English. Provide original and translated documents in your application. Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters. Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their: full name. address and telephone number. qualifications and experience in the language they are translating. These details must be in English. Note: You do not need to have any documents certified.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Scan or photograph: Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour. The scans and photos must be clear. If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Travel after you apply
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Travel after you apply: If you are in Australia, you don't have to tell us if you want to travel outside Australia while we process your application. This is because you can be outside Australia when we decide on your application. If you leave Australia, you must make sure you have a valid visa to return. Learn about visa expiry. Learn about Bridging visas.

abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Biometrics: We might ask for biometrics (fingerprints and photo). We will let you know if you need to provide them.

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Stay lawful
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Stay lawful: Make sure you stay lawful by holding a valid visa while we process your application. When you apply for this visa in Australia, you are likely to be granted a bridging visa. If your current visa expires before we decide your application, the bridging visa will start. You can stay in Australia on the bridging visa while we process your new visa application. Learn more about visa expiry.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Pay the second instalment
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Pay the second instalment: If you need to pay a second instalment, we will send you an invoice after you have met all other requirements for the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Add family
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Add family: You can add family members to your application after you apply but before we decide on your visa. For this visa your family members are: your partner. your dependent child. your partner’s dependent child.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Help with your application: Let us know if you no longer want someone to: receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person. Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount. For more information see Who can help you with your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Tell us if things change
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Tell us if things change: Tell us if things change after you submit your application but before we decide on your application. Things you need to let us know about include: you want to withdraw your application. changes to your phone number, address or passport. changes to your relationship status. the birth of a child. See what to do if your situation changes.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream: Visa outcome
abstract: Employer Nomination Scheme visa (subclass 186), Direct Entry stream, Visa outcome: You can be inside or outside Australia when we decide on your visa application. We must have approved your employer’s nomination before we can grant you this visa. We will let you know our decision about your visa application in writing. If we grant your visa, we will tell you: your visa grant number. the date your visa starts. your visa conditions. Keep a copy of the decision. If we refuse your visa, we will tell you: why we refused the visa. whether you have a right to a review of the decision. We will not refund the visa application charge if we refuse your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: With this visa you can
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, With this visa you can: live, work and study only in designated regional areas of Australia for 5 years. travel to and from Australia for 5 years. if eligible, apply for permanent residence after 3 years from the time we grant your visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: How long you can stay
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, How long you can stay: 5 years.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: Cost
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, Cost: Concessions apply in limited circumstances. Cost Concession. From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application. See About this visa. To see what your visa will cost use the Visa pricing estimator. The estimator does not consider the second instalment or other costs.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: You must
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, You must: have a nomination to work in an occupation on the relevant skilled occupation list. have at least 3 years relevant work experience in your nominated occupation. have a relevant skills assessment, unless an exemption applies. work only for your sponsor or associated entity, unless an exemption applies. be under 45 years of age, unless an exemption applies. meet minimum standards of English language proficiency. Help with your visa. If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: Be this age
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, Be this age: You must be under 45 years of age when you apply for the visa. You are exempt from this criteria if any of the following applies to you: You are nominated as an academic (University Lecturer or Faculty Head at Academic Level A, B, C, D or E) by a university in Australia. You are nominated as a medical practitioner and in the 3 years immediately before you apply have worked in that occupation in a designated regional area of Australia for 2 years as the holder of a Temporary Work (Skilled) visa (subclass 457) or subclass 482 visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: Be this age
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, Be this age: The nominated position is in a designated regional area of Australia. You are nominated as a scientist, researcher or technical (scientific) specialist at ANZSCO skill level 1 or 2 by an Australian scientific government agency or Australian university. You have held a Special Category visa (subclass 444) or New Zealand Citizen Family Relationship visa (subclass 461) visa for the last 3 years immediately before you apply and have worked for the employer who nominated you, in the nominated occupation, for at least 2 years during that time.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: Be this age
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, Be this age: As a subclass 457 or 482 visa holder, you have been working in the nominated occupation for the nominating employer for a period of at least 2 years during the 3 years ending immediately before you apply, and your earnings for each year of that period were at least as much as the Fair Work High Income Threshold.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: Be nominated by an approved sponsor
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, Be nominated by an approved sponsor: You must be nominated by an employer whose business is lawfully operating in Australia. You must be employed to work in the nominated occupation and in a position within the sponsoring business or an associated entity of that business, located in a designated regional area of Australia. Before you can apply for the visa, your employer will need to lodge a nomination application for you. They will only be able to do this if they are an approved work sponsor or have at least lodged an application to become a standard business sponsor.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: Have relevant skills, qualifications and work experience
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, Have relevant skills, qualifications and work experience: If you are the primary visa applicant, you must show that you have the skills, qualifications and work experience necessary to perform the nominated occupation. You must undertake a skills assessment to show this – see Have a positive skills assessment below. If it is not mandatory for you to undertake a skills assessment, you are still required to provide other evidence to show that you meet this requirement – see ' Skills and qualifications documents '.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: Have relevant skills, qualifications and work experience
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, Have relevant skills, qualifications and work experience: You must have been employed in the nominated occupation for at least 3 years on a full-time basis and at the skill level required for the nominated occupation. Generally, you should have gained your experience within the last 5 years. The period does not need to be continuous. We might consider equivalent part-time work. We do not consider casual work.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: Have a positive skills assessment
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, Have a positive skills assessment: You must have your skills assessed as suitable for the nominated occupation by the relevant assessing authority. The assessment will show us you have the skills to work in the nominated occupation. The skills assessment must be undertaken before your application is lodged. A skills assessment obtained for a Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) is not a valid assessment for this visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream: Have a positive skills assessment
abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, Have a positive skills assessment: You do not need to complete a skills assessment if at the time of application you held a Temporary Work (Skilled) visa (subclass 457) or subclass 482 for the nominated occupation and in order to be granted that visa, you were required to demonstrate your skills by providing a suitable skills assessment.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 494), Employer Sponsored stream, Have a positive skills assessment: You are exempt from this criteria if any of the following applies to you: you are nominated as an academic (University Lecturer or Faculty Head at academic Level A, B, C, D or E) by an Australian university. you have held a Special Category visa (subclass 444) or New Zealand Citizen Family Relationship visa (subclass 461) visa for the last 3 years immediately before you apply and have worked for the employer who nominated you, in the nominated occupation, for at least 2 years during that time.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Apply as a retiree: You can apply for a Parent visa (subclass 103) as a retiree if: on 8 May 2018, you held or had previously held an Investor Retirement (subclass 405) visa or Retirement (subclass 410), and. you have not held any other substantive visa between 8 May 2018 and the date you applied for the Parent visa, and. you are in Australia. If you apply for this visa as a retiree: you do not need to meet the balance of family test. you do not need to have an Assurance of Support. you do not need a sponsor.

abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Meet the balance of family test: You must meet the balance of family test. For more information and examples of how the test is applied, visit balance of family test. If you apply for this visa as a retiree, you do not need to meet the balance of family test.

abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Have Assurance of Support: You must be able to obtain an Assurance of Support, unless you apply for the visa as a retiree under the Retirement visa pathway. The assurance is for you and any family members who come to Australia with you on this visa. We will let you know when you need to provide the Assurance of Support. The sponsor or a family member does not need to provide An Assurance of Support.

attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Identity documents
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Identity documents: Documents that prove a change of name include: a marriage or divorce certificate. change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority. documents that show other names you have been known by.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Sponsor documents
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Sponsor documents: An eligible sponsor must sponsor your application, unless you are applying as a retiree. Your sponsor must complete Form 40 Sponsorship for migration to Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Balance of family documents
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Balance of family documents: You must show us that you meet the balance of family test. You can show this by giving us: evidence of how you are related to each child. evidence of each child's Australian citizenship or country of permanent residence. evidence that your child should not be included in the balance of family test (for example, their death certificate). You do not need to meet the balance of family test if you are applying as a retiree.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Character documents
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Character documents: We might ask you for character documents, including police certificates. Do not arrange a police check until we ask you to. Learn more about Character requirements for visas.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Assurance of Support
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Assurance of Support: When we ask for it, provide us with an Assurance of Support. The sponsor or a family member does not need to provide an Assurance of Support. An individual, more than one person, or an organisation can provide it. Learn more about Assurances of Support. You do not need to provide an Assurance of Support if you are applying as a retiree.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Tell us you are getting help
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Tell us you are getting help: To nominate someone to: receive your correspondence, complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. give you immigration assistance, complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Dependants under 18 documents
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Dependants under 18 documents: For every dependant under 18 years old who is applying with you, provide: identity documents. evidence of your relationship with them, for example, a birth or marriage certificate. character documents, if applicable. If you are applying as a retiree, you cannot include your children or your partner's children in your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Parental responsibility documents
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Parental responsibility documents: You must get consent for any applicant under 18 years of age to migrate to Australia from anyone who: has a legal right to decide where the child lives, and. is not coming to Australia with the child. They must complete either: Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years. a statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to visit Australia on this visa. Alternatively, you can show us: an Australian court order that allows your child to migrate to Australia, or. that the laws of your home country allow them to migrate.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Parental responsibility documents
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Parental responsibility documents: You must include: an identity document that shows the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, for example, a passport or driver’s licence. adoption papers or other court documents, if applicable.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Dependants over 18 documents: To be included in your visa application as a dependent child, your child must be: under 18 years of age. over 18 years of age but not yet turned 23, and dependent on you or your partner. over 23 years of age, unable to earn a living to support themselves due to physical or cognitive limitations, and dependent on you or your partner.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Dependants over 18 documents: For every dependant 18 years of age or older who is applying with you, provide: identity documents. evidence of your relationship with them, for example, a birth or marriage certificate. documents about their other relationships, if applicable. character documents. proof of dependency. If your child is likely to turn 23 while we process your application, you will need to provide evidence they are dependent on you due to disability. For more information on visa processing times, see Parent visa queue release dates.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Dependants over 18 documents: If you are applying as a retiree, you cannot include your children, or your partner's children, in your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Proof of dependency
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Proof of dependency: You need to prove that this person is dependent on you. You must provide: a completed Form 47A - Details of a child or other dependent family member aged 18 years or over. proof of your relationship with the dependant, for example, a birth certificate or adoption papers. You must also prove this person has been financially dependent on you for at least 12 months before you apply. You could provide: proof they live with you. their tax records. proof they are currently studying.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Partner documents
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Partner documents: Provide us with: identity documents. character documents. evidence of your relationship with them, for example your current marriage certificate or documents that prove you have been in a de facto relationship for at least 12 months before you apply. documents about other relationships, if applicable. Documents that prove your de facto relationship include: joint bank account statements. billing accounts in joint names. joint leases or mortgages. documents that show you have lived at the same address as your partner.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Photographs
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Photographs: Provide 4 recent photos of anyone included in the application. Photographs must be: passport-size (45mm x 35mm). less than 6 months old. good quality colour - we will not accept laser copies. a view of your full face. taken against a plain light-coloured background. You can wear untinted prescription glasses. If you wear a head covering for religious reasons, you can show only your face.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Translate
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Translate: Have all non-English documents translated into English. You must give us original certified copies and translated documents in your application. Translators in Australia should be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters. Translators outside Australia do not need to be accredited, but on each translation, they must include their: full name. address and telephone number. qualifications and experience in the language they are translating. These details must be in English.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Certify
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Certify: Do not certify police certificates. You must give us the original documents. All other documents must be certified copies. This includes: non-English documents. English translations.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Keep

attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Send
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Send: Send us: original police certificates. certified copies of all other documents. as much relevant information as possible to help us make a decision on your application. each document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing. all documents with your application, if you can.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Apply for the visa
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Apply for the visa: Apply for the visa online. You can be in or outside Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when you submit your application. If you are applying as a retiree, you must be in Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when you submit your application. You can be in or outside Australia when we make our decision. You cannot apply for this visa if you have already applied for or hold a Sponsored Parent (Temporary) (subclass 870) visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Apply online using ImmiAccount
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Apply online using ImmiAccount: If you apply on or after 22 April 2026, you must lodge an online application using ImmiAccount: Create an account or log in to ImmiAccount. Attach documents. Pay the application fee. If you cannot apply online due to a technical issue, please submit an ImmiAccount Technical Support Form. If technical support does not resolve the issue, we will consider allowing you to submit a paper application. Using our website and protections to your privacy. We take our obligation to protect your privacy seriously.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Apply online using ImmiAccount
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Apply online using ImmiAccount: We provide a secure online environment, but you can do more to ensure your personal safety online: Make sure you give us your contact details when you apply for your visa and tell us if they have changed. We may need to contact you directly, even if you have: nominated your sponsor's email address for all electronic correspondence. appointed your sponsor or someone else to receive your correspondence as your authorised recipient. appointed someone to give you immigration assistance. Protect your email account, passwords and ImmiAccount. Do not share them with anyone.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): After you apply
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), After you apply: We will let you know when we have received your application and documents. There may be other things you need to know and might need to do.

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Importing your paper application
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Importing your paper application: Applicants who have submitted a paper application can import it into ImmiAccount. You can do this after you receive your acknowledgement letter. Importing your application into ImmiAccount gives you access to online services. This makes it easier to manage your application. You can use our online services in ImmiAccount to: attach supporting documents to your application. view messages we send you. update your details. view the status of your application. Follow these steps to import your application: Create a new ImmiAccount or log into your existing ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Importing your paper application
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Importing your paper application: See instructions on how to use ImmiAccount. For more information, see Apply and Manage your application in ImmiAccount. You can import any Parent (subclass 103) visa applications lodged after November 2018.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Health exams

attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Add family members
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Add family members: You might be able to add family members to your application before we make a decision. If you have submitted your application online, or imported your application into ImmiAccount, you can use ImmiAccount to upload the form. Alternatively, you can send us the form using the Parent visa processing centre form. You will also need to give us evidence of your relationship and a copy of the family member's passport.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Add family members
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Add family members: If you want to add a spouse or de facto partner to your application, they can be in or outside Australia when you add them unless you applied as a retiree. If you want to add a dependent child to your application, they can be in or outside Australia when you add them.

Alternatively, you can send us the form using the Parent visa processing centre form.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Help with your application
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Help with your application: Tell us if you no longer want someone to: receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. provide immigration assistance - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person. attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Tell us if things change
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Tell us if things change: You need to tell us about changes to your: phone number. email. address. passport. relationship status. family composition, including the birth of a child. You should also tell us if you want to withdraw your application. See what to do if your situation changes.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Withdraw your application and apply for a different visa
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Withdraw your application and apply for a different visa: Other parent visas might be processed more quickly including the: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143). This is a permanent visa. Contributory Parent visas may be processed faster, but it costs more than a Parent visa (subclass 103). Contributory Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 173) followed by a permanent Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143). This 2-step visa process is faster but costs more than the Parent visa (subclass 103). It also costs more than applying directly for the Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), but the cost is spread across the 2 visas over a longer period.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Withdraw your application and apply for a different visa
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Withdraw your application and apply for a different visa: If you switch to one of these Contributory Parent visas, we will take the date you originally applied for a subclass 103 visa into account for your new application. Switching to a Contributory Parent visa application will not disadvantage you. Not all applicants who applied for the subclass 103 visa need to apply for a contributory visa. If one applicant for the subclass 103 visa changes their application, it will not affect the other application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Stay lawful
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Stay lawful: If you are in Australia and your current temporary visa is about to expire, you should make sure you stay lawful by holding a valid visa while we process your application. You are not entitled to a bridging visa associated with your subclass 103 visa application unless you are applying under the Retirement visa pathway. If your current visa expires before we make a decision on your application, the bridging visa will start. You must be outside Australia while we process your visa application, unless you hold another valid visa. Learn about visa expiry.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Visa outcome
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Visa outcome: New step description.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Parent visa (subclass 103): Visa outcome
abstract: Parent visa (subclass 103), Visa outcome: You must be outside Australia when we make a decision on your application. If you apply as a retiree, you may be in or outside Australia when we make a decision on your application. We will let you know our decision in writing. If we grant you the visa, we will let you know: your visa grant number. the date your visa starts. your visa conditions. You should keep a copy of our decision. If we refuse your visa, we will tell you: why we refused the visa. if you have a right to a review of the decision. We will not refund the application fee if we refuse your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): With this visa you can
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), With this visa you can: stay in Australia indefinitely. work and study in Australia. enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme called Medicare. sponsor your family members to come to Australia. travel to and from Australia for 5 years. if eligible, attend free English language classes provided by the Adult Migrant English Program. if eligible, apply for Australian citizenship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): How long you can stay
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), How long you can stay: Permanently.

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Cost
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Cost: From AUD49,900 over 2 instalments for a single applicant. Concessions apply in limited circumstances. Costs may be lower for Contributory Parent (Temporary) (subclass 173) and substituted Visitor (subclass 600) visa holders. For more information on additional fees that may apply, go to the ‘About this Visa’ page and click on Cost. Cost concession. From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application. See About this visa tab.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): You must
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), You must: have an eligible child who is a settled Australian citizen, Australian Permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen. meet all applicable visa conditions and follow Australian law. not have already applied for or hold a Sponsored Parent (Temporary) (subclass 870) visa when applying for this visa. Help with your visa. If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Not have this visa
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Not have this visa: You cannot apply for this visa if you have already applied for or hold a Sponsored Parent (Temporary) (subclass 870) visa.

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Apply as a Contributory Parent (Temporary) visa holder
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Apply as a Contributory Parent (Temporary) visa holder: You can apply for the Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143) second stage Permanent pathway option if: you hold a Contributory Parent (Temporary) (subclass 173) visa when you apply, or. you held a Contributory Parent (Temporary) (subclass 173) visa any time in the 28 days before applying, or. more than 28 days have passed since your Contributory Parent (Temporary) (subclass 173) visa ended, and you can demonstrate compelling and compassionate circumstances to regain your previous visa status. You must provide evidence and the Minister must be satisfied these circumstances exist.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Apply as a Contributory Parent (Temporary) visa holder
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Apply as a Contributory Parent (Temporary) visa holder: If none of these options apply to you, we will process your Contributory Parent (subclass 143) application as a standard application, and not the 2-stage pathway. If you apply for this visa as a Contributory Parent (Temporary) visa holder, you have already met the balance of family test.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Apply as a retiree
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Apply as a retiree: You can apply for a Parent visa (subclass 143) as a retiree if: on 8 May 2018, you held or had previously held an Investor Retirement (subclass 405) visa or Retirement (subclass 410), and. you have not held any other substantive visa between 8 May 2018 and the date you applied for the Parent visa, and. you are in Australia. If you apply for this visa as a retiree: you do not need to meet the balance of family test. you do not need to have an assurance of support. you do not need a sponsor.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Have a sponsor
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Have a sponsor: You must have an eligible sponsor. Usually, an eligible child will sponsor you. If your child is under 18, an eligible relative or community organisation can sponsor you. We must approve the sponsorship. For more information on eligible sponsors, change the switch at the top right of the page to ‘Sponsors'. If you apply for this visa as a retiree, you do not need a sponsor. If your sponsor dies. If you hold a Temporary Contributory Parent (subclass 173) visa, you might still be eligible for this visa if your sponsor dies. See what to do if your situation changes.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Meet the balance of family test
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Meet the balance of family test: You must meet the balance of family test. You meet the test if: at least half of your children and step-children are eligible children, or. there are more eligible children living in Australia than any other single country. For more information and examples of how the test is applied, visit balance of family test. If you apply for this visa as a retiree you do not need to meet the balance of family test. If you hold a Contributory Parent (subclass 173) (Temporary) visa, you have already met the balance of family test.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Have Assurance of Support
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Have Assurance of Support: You must be able to obtain an Assurance of Support, unless you apply for the visa as a retiree under the Retirement visa pathway. An Assurance of Support guarantees us that you will not need to rely on government assistance after you enter Australia on this visa for the Assurance of Support period. The assurance is for you and any family members who come to Australia with you on this visa. We will let you know when you need to provide the Assurance of Support. The sponsor or a family member does not need to provide An Assurance of Support.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Not have had a visa cancelled or a previous application refused: We will consider your immigration history when we make a decision on your application. attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Sign the Australian Values Statement
