attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Contributory Parent (subclass 173) visa holders
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Contributory Parent (subclass 173) visa holders: You will not need to give us some of the documents we usually ask for if: you hold a subclass 173 visa, or. your subclass 173 visa ended in the 28 days immediately before you apply for this visa. You will still need to provide documents: to let us know you are getting help with your application. if there has been a change in your situation since we granted you the 173 visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Contributory Parent (subclass 173) visa holders
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Contributory Parent (subclass 173) visa holders: Changes in your situation that we need evidence of include: your family member is no longer a dependant. your partner relationship has changed. you have had a baby. your contact details have changed. you have a new passport. you want to nominate a new sponsor. your sponsor has died.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Identity documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Identity documents: We need proof of your identity. If you cannot prove your identity: we will refuse your visa application. we might not grant you another visa for 10 years. we might not grant any family members you listed on your application a visa for 10 years. Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates. Also provide: a national identity card, if you have one. proof of change of name, if applicable.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Identity documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Identity documents: Documents that prove a change of name include: a marriage or divorce certificate. change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority. documents that show other names you have been known by.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Sponsor documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Sponsor documents: An eligible sponsor must sponsor your application, unless you are applying as a retiree. Your sponsor must complete Form 40 Sponsorship for migration to Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Balance of family documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Balance of family documents: You must show us that you meet the balance of family test. You can show this by giving us: evidence of how you are related to each child. evidence of each child's Australian citizenship or country of permanent residence. evidence that your child should not be included in the balance of family test (for example, their death certificate). You do not need to meet the balance of family test if you are applying as a retiree. If you hold a Contributory Parent (subclass 173) visa, you have already met the balance of family test.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Character documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Character documents: We might ask you for character documents, including police certificates. Do not arrange a police check until we ask you to. Learn more about police certificates.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Assurance of Support documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Assurance of Support documents: When we ask for it, provide us with an Assurance of Support. The sponsor or a family member does not need to provide an Assurance of Support. An individual, more than one person, or an organisation can provide it. Learn more about Assurances of Support. You do not need to provide an Assurance of Support if you are applying as a retiree.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Tell us you are getting help
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Tell us you are getting help: To nominate someone to: receive your correspondence, complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. give you immigration assistance, complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Dependants under 18 documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Dependants under 18 documents: For every dependant under 18 years old who is applying with you, provide: identity documents. evidence of your relationship with them, for example, a birth or marriage certificate. character documents, if applicable. If you are applying as a retiree, you cannot include your children or your partner's children in your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Parental responsibility documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Parental responsibility documents: You must get consent for any applicant under 18 years of age to migrate to Australia from anyone who: has a legal right to decide where the child lives, and. is not coming to Australia with the child. They must complete either: Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years or. a statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to visit Australia on this visa. Alternatively, you can show us: an Australian court order that allows your child to migrate to Australia, or. that the laws of your home country allow them to migrate.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Parental responsibility documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Parental responsibility documents: You must include: an identity document that shows the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, for example, a passport or driver’s licence. adoption papers or other court documents, if applicable.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Dependants over 18 documents: To be included in your visa application as a dependent child, your child must be: under 18 years of age. over 18 years of age but not yet turned 23, and dependent on you or your partner. over 23 years of age, unable to earn a living to support themselves due to physical or cognitive limitations, and dependent on you or your partner.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Dependants over 18 documents: For every dependant 18 years of age or older who is applying with you, provide: identity documents. evidence of your relationship with them, for example, a birth or marriage certificate. documents about their other relationships, if applicable. character documents. proof of dependency. If your child is likely to turn 23 while we process your application, you will need to provide evidence they are dependent on you due to disability. For more information on visa processing times, see Parent visa queue release dates.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Dependants over 18 documents: If you are applying as a retiree, you cannot include your children, or your partner's children, in your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Proof of dependency
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Proof of dependency: You need to prove that this person is dependent on you. You must provide: a completed Form 47A Details of a child or other dependent family member aged 18 years or over. proof of your relationship with the dependant, for example, a birth certificate or adoption papers. You must also prove this person has been financially dependent on you for at least 12 months before you apply. You could provide: proof they live with you. their tax records. proof they are currently studying.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Partner documents
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Partner documents: Provide us with: identity documents. character documents. evidence of your relationship with them, for example your current marriage certificate or documents that prove you have been in a de facto relationship for at least 12 months before you apply. documents about other relationships, if applicable. Documents that prove your de facto relationship include: joint bank account statements. billing accounts in joint names. joint leases or mortgages. documents that show you have lived at the same address as your partner.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Photographs
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Photographs: Provide 4 recent photos of anyone included in the application. Photographs must be: passport-size (45mm x 35mm). less than 6 months old. good quality colour – we will not accept laser copies. a view of your full face. taken against a plain light-coloured background. You can wear untinted prescription glasses. If you wear a head covering for religious reasons, you can show only your face.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Translate
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Translate: Have all non-English documents translated into English. You must give us original certified copies and translated documents in your application. Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters. Translators outside Australia do not need to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their: full name. address and telephone number. qualifications and experience in the language they are translating. These details must be in English.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Certify
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Certify: Do not certify police certificates. You must give us the original documents. All other documents must be certified copies. This includes: non-English documents. English translations.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Keep
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Keep: Keep a copy of your completed application, including all supporting documents.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Send
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Send: Send us: original police certificates. certified copies of all other documents. as much relevant information as possible to help us make a decision on your application. each document only once, even if you are using to show more than one thing. all documents with your application, if you can.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Apply for the visa
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Apply for the visa: Apply for the visa online. You can be in or outside Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when you submit your application. If you are applying as a retiree, you must be in Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when you submit your application. You can be in or outside Australia when we make our decision. You cannot apply for this visa if you have already applied for or hold a Sponsored Parent (Temporary) (subclass 870) visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Apply online using ImmiAccount
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Apply online using ImmiAccount: If you apply on or after 22 April 2026, you must lodge an online application using ImmiAccount: Create an account or log in to ImmiAccount. Attach documents. Pay the application fee. If you cannot apply online due to a technical issue, please submit an ImmiAccount Technical Support Form. If technical support does not resolve the issue, we will consider allowing you to submit a paper application. Using our website and protections to your privacy. We take our obligation to protect your privacy seriously.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Apply online using ImmiAccount
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Apply online using ImmiAccount: We provide a secure online environment, but you can do more to ensure your personal safety online: Make sure you give us your contact details when you apply for your visa and tell us if they have changed. We may need to contact you directly, even if you have: nominated your sponsor's email address for all electronic correspondence. appointed your sponsor or someone else to receive your correspondence as your authorised recipient. appointed someone to give you immigration assistance. Protect your email account, passwords and ImmiAccount. Do not share them with anyone.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): After you apply
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), After you apply: We will let you know when we have received your application and documents. There may be other things you need to know and might need to do.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Importing your paper application
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Importing your paper application: Applicants who have submitted a paper application can import it into ImmiAccount. You can do this after you receive your acknowledgement letter. Importing your application into ImmiAccount gives you access to online services. This makes it easier to manage your application. You can use our online services in ImmiAccount to: attach supporting documents to your application. view messages we send you. update your details. view the status of your application. Follow these steps to import your application: Create a new ImmiAccount or log into your existing ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Importing your paper application
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Importing your paper application: See instructions on how to use ImmiAccount. Once you log in, import your application by entering your: application ID. date of birth. identity document number (ImmiCard, passport or Titre de Voyage number). For more information, see Apply and Manage your application in ImmiAccount. You can import any Parent (subclass 103) visa applications lodged after November 2018.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Status updates
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Status updates: We cannot provide updates on your application's progress within normal processing times. We will let you know if you need to give us anything more. Learn more about processing times at Parent visa queue release dates.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): If you applied in Australia
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), If you applied in Australia: If you hold a visa that allows you to be in Australia when we make a decision on your visa application, you do not need to tell us if you want to travel outside Australia. If you leave Australia, make sure you have a valid visa to return. Learn about visa expiry.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): If you applied outside Australia
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), If you applied outside Australia: Do not arrange to move to Australia permanently until we let you know in writing that we have granted you the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Health exams
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Health exams: We will let you know when you need to complete health examinations.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Biometrics
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Biometrics: We might ask for biometrics (fingerprints and photos). We will let you know if you need to provide them.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Send more information
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Send more information: We might also ask you to provide more information. If you submitted your application online or imported it into ImmiAccount, you can use ImmiAccount to upload more documents that you did not send with your application. Alternatively, you can send us additional documents using the Parent visa processing centre form.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Pay the second instalment
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Pay the second instalment: You must pay the second instalment before we will grant the visa. We will send you an invoice when it is due. If you do not pay the invoice, we will refuse your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Add family members
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Add family members: You might be able to add family members to your application before we make a decision. Complete and send us Form 1436 Adding an additional applicant after lodgement. If you have submitted your application online, or imported your application into ImmiAccount, you can use ImmiAccount to upload the form. Alternatively, you can send us the form using the Parent visa processing centre form. You will also need to give us evidence of your relationship and a copy of the family member's passport.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Add family members
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Add family members: If you want to add a spouse or de facto partner to your application, they can be in or outside Australia when you add them unless you applied as a retiree. If you applied as a retiree, your spouse or de facto partner must be in Australia when you add them. If you want to add a dependent child to your application, they can be in or outside Australia when you add them.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Newborn child
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Newborn child: Find out what to do if you had a child.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Mistakes on your application
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Mistakes on your application: Tell us as soon as you can if you make a mistake on your application. To do this, complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers. If you have submitted your application online, or imported your application into ImmiAccount, you can use ImmiAccount to upload the form. Alternatively, you can send us the form using the Parent visa processing centre form.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Help with your application
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Help with your application: Tell us if you no longer want someone to: receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. provide immigration assistance - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person. If you have submitted your application online, or imported your application into ImmiAccount, you can use ImmiAccount to upload the form. Alternatively, you can send us the form using the Parent visa processing centre form. For more information see Who can help you with your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Tell us if things change
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Tell us if things change: You need to tell us about changes to your: phone number. email. address. passport. relationship status. family composition, including the birth of a child. You should also tell us if you want to withdraw your application. See what to do if your situation changes.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Stay lawful
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Stay lawful: If you are in Australia and your current temporary visa is about to expire, you should make sure you stay lawful by holding a valid visa while we process your application. You are not entitled to a bridging visa associated with your subclass 143 visa application unless: you are applying under the Retirement visa pathway. you held a Contributory Parent (Temporary) (subclass 173) visa when you applied, or. you are a family member of a Contributory Parent (Temporary) (subclass 173) visa holder.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Stay lawful
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Stay lawful: You must be outside Australia while we process your visa application, unless you hold another valid visa. Learn about visa expiry.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Visa outcome ​
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Visa outcome ​: New step description.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Visa outcome ​
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Visa outcome ​: You may be in or outside Australia when we make a decision on your application if: you applied as a retiree, or. you hold or held a Contributory Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 173), or a substituted Visitor visa (subclass 600), before submitting your application. All other Contributory Parent applicants must be outside Australia when we make a decision on your application. We will let you know our decision in writing. If we grant you the visa, we will let you know: your visa grant number. the date your visa starts. your visa conditions. You should keep a copy of our decision.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143): Visa outcome ​
abstract: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), Visa outcome ​: If we refuse your visa, we will tell you: why we refused the visa. if you have a right to a review of the decision. We will not refund the application fee if we refuse your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): With this visa you can
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), With this visa you can: stay in Australia indefinitely. work and study in Australia. enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme called Medicare. sponsor your family members to come to Australia. travel to and from Australia for 5 years. If eligible, attend free English language classes provided by the Adult Migrant English Program. if eligible, apply for Australian citizenship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): How long you can stay
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), How long you can stay: Permanently.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Cost
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Cost: From AUD8,665 over 2 instalments for a single applicant. Concessions apply in limited circumstances. For more information on additional fees that may apply, go to the ‘About this visa’ page and click on Costs. Cost concession. From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application. See About this visa tab.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): You must
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), You must: have an eligible child who is a settled Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen. be old enough to receive the age pension in Australia. not have already applied for or hold a Sponsored Parent (Temporary) (subclass 870) visa when applying for this visa. Help with your visa. If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Not have this visa
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Not have this visa: You cannot apply for this visa if you have already applied for or hold a Sponsored Parent (Temporary) (subclass 870) visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Have a sponsor
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Have a sponsor: You must have an eligible sponsor. Usually, an eligible child will sponsor you. If your child is under 18, an eligible relative or community organisation can sponsor you. We must approve the sponsorship. For more information on eligible sponsors, change the switch at the top right of the page to 'Sponsors'.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Be this age
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Be this age: You must be old enough to receive the age pension in Australia. For more information on the age pension, visit Older Australians.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Have Assurance of Support
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Have Assurance of Support: You must be able to obtain an Assurance of Support, unless you apply for the visa as a retiree under the Retirement visa pathway. An Assurance of Support guarantees us that you will not need to rely on government assistance after you enter Australia on this visa for the Assurance of Support period. The assurance is for you and any family members who come to Australia with you on this visa. We will let you know when you need to provide the Assurance of Support. The sponsor or a family member does not need to provide An Assurance of Support.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Have Assurance of Support
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Have Assurance of Support: An individual, more than one person, or an organisation can provide it. Learn more about Assurances of Support.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Meet the health requirement
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Meet the health requirement: You and any family members who apply for the visa with you must meet our health requirement. We might also ask that other non-migrating family members meet the requirement.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Meet the character requirement
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Meet the character requirement: You and any family members who apply for the visa with you, must meet our character requirement. We might also ask that other non-migrating family members meet the requirement.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Meet the balance of family test
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Meet the balance of family test: You must meet the balance of family test. You meet the test if: at least half of your children and step-children are eligible children, or. there are more eligible children living in Australia than in any other single country. For more information and examples of how the test is applied, visit balance of family test.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Have paid back your debt to the Australian government
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Have paid back your debt to the Australian government: If you or any family members owe the Australian Government money, the debt must be paid back, or there must be an approved arrangement to pay it back.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Not have had a visa cancelled or a previous application refused
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Not have had a visa cancelled or a previous application refused: We will consider your immigration history when we make a decision on your application. This means you might not be eligible for this visa if you have had a visa cancelled or refused before. In some circumstances you may still apply for a permanent visa if you have had a visa cancelled or an application refused. For more information, see Limitations on applications in Australia. If you are applying for a visa from outside Australia, see Can I go to Australia. If you would like immigration assistance, see Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Sign the Australian Values Statement
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Sign the Australian Values Statement: If you are 18 years of age or older, you must: have read, or had explained to you, the Life in Australia booklet. sign an Australian Values Statement. This is to confirm that you will respect the Australian way of life and obey Australian laws.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Best interests of the child
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Best interests of the child: We will not grant this visa if it is not in the best interests of an applicant under 18.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Before you apply
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Before you apply: Check your passport. If you need help with your application, get someone to act on your behalf.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Check your passport
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Check your passport: You and anyone who applies for the visa with you must have valid passports before we grant the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Get help with your application
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Get help with your application: Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance, they must be: a registered migration agent. a legal practitioner, or. an exempt person. You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter. To learn more, see authorised recipients.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): If you have an existing Parent visa application
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), If you have an existing Parent visa application: If you have applied for a different Parent visa but we have not made a decision on it, you must withdraw that application when you apply for this visa. You can do this as part of your new application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Gather your documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Gather your documents: Gather all your documents, including those for any partner or dependents who are applying with you. You will also need your sponsor documents.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Provide accurate documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Provide accurate documents: There are consequences if you do not give us accurate or complete information. To learn more, see providing accurate information.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Identity documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Identity documents: We need proof of your identity. If you cannot prove your identity: we will refuse your visa application. we might not grant you another visa for 10 years. we might not grant any family members you listed on your application a visa for 10 years. Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates. Also provide: a national identity card, if you have one. proof of change of name, if applicable.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Identity documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Identity documents: Documents that prove a change of name include: a marriage or divorce certificate. change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority. documents that show other names you have been known by.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Sponsor documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Sponsor documents: An eligible sponsor must sponsor your application. Your sponsor must complete Form 40 Sponsorship for migration to Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Balance of family documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Balance of family documents: You must show us that you meet the balance of family test. You can show this by giving us: evidence of how you are related to each child. evidence of each child's Australian citizenship or country of permanent residence. evidence that your child should not be included in the balance of family test (for example, their death certificate).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Character documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Character documents: We might ask you for character documents including police certificates. Do not arrange a police check until we ask you to. Learn more about police certificates.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Assurance of support
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Assurance of support: When we ask for it, provide us with an Assurance of Support. The sponsor or a family member does not need to provide an Assurance of Support. An individual, more than one person, or an organisation can provide it. You do not need to provide an Assurance of Support if you are applying as a retiree. Learn more about Assurances of Support.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Tell us you are getting help
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Tell us you are getting help: To nominate someone to: receive your correspondence, complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. give you immigration assistance, complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Dependants under 18 documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Dependants under 18 documents: For every dependant under 18 years old who is applying with you, provide: identity documents. evidence of your relationship with them, for example, a birth or marriage certificate. character documents, if applicable. If you are applying as a retiree, you cannot include your children or your partner's children in your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Parental responsibility documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Parental responsibility documents: You must get consent for any applicant under 18 years of age to migrate to Australia from anyone who: has a legal right to decide where the child lives, and. is not coming to Australia with the child. They must complete either: Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years; or. a statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to visit Australia on this visa. Alternatively, you can show us: an Australian court order that allows your child to migrate to Australia, or. that the laws of your home country allow them to migrate.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Parental responsibility documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Parental responsibility documents: You must include: an identity document that shows the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, for example, a passport or driver’s licence. adoption papers or other court documents, if applicable.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Dependants over 18 documents: To be included in your visa application as a dependent child, your child must be: under 18 years of age. over 18 years of age but not yet turned 23, and dependent on you or your partner. over 23 years of age, unable to earn a living to support themselves due to physical or cognitive limitations and dependent on you or your partner.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Dependants over 18 documents: For every dependant 18 years of age or older who is applying with you, provide: identity documents. evidence of your relationship with them, for example, a birth or marriage certificate. documents about their other relationships, if applicable. character documents. proof of dependency. If your child is likely to turn 23 while we process your application, you will need to provide evidence they are dependent on you due to disability. For more information on visa processing times, see Parent visa queue release dates.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Dependants over 18 documents: If you are applying as a retiree, you cannot include your children or your partner's children in your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Proof of dependency
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Proof of dependency: You need to prove that this person is dependent on you. You must provide: a completed Form 47A Details of a child or other dependent family member aged 18 years or over. proof of your relationship with the dependant, for example, a birth certificate or adoption papers. You must also prove this person has been financially dependent on you for at least 12 months before you apply. You could provide: proof they live with you. their tax records. proof they are currently studying.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Partner documents
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Partner documents: Provide us with: identity documents. character documents. evidence of your relationship with them, for example your current marriage certificate or documents that prove you have been in a de facto relationship for at least 12 months before you apply. documents about other relationships, if applicable. Documents that prove your de facto relationship include: joint bank account statements. billing accounts in joint names. joint leases or mortgages. documents that show you have lived at the same address as your partner.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Photographs
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Photographs: Provide 4 recent photos of anyone included in the application. Photographs must be: passport-size (45mm x 35mm). less than 6 months old. good quality colour - we will not accept laser copies. a view of your full face. taken against a plain light-coloured background. You can wear untinted prescription glasses. If you wear a head covering for religious reasons, you can show only your face.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Translate
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Translate: Have all non-English documents translated into English. You must give us original certified copies and translated documents in your application. Translators in Australia should be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters. Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited, but on each translation, they must include their: full name. address and telephone number. qualifications and experience in the language they are translating. These details must be in English.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Certify
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Certify: Do not certify police certificates. You must give us the original documents. All other documents must be certified copies. This includes: non-English documents. English translations.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Keep
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Keep: Keep a copy of your completed application, including all supporting documents.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Send
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Send: Send us: original police certificates. certified copies of all other documents. as much information as possible to help us make a decision on your application. each document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing. all documents with your application, if you can.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Apply for the visa
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Apply for the visa: Apply for the visa online. You can be in or outside Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when you submit your application. If you are applying as a retiree, you must be in Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when you submit your application. You can be in or outside Australia when we make our decision. You cannot apply for this visa if you have already applied for or hold a Sponsored Parent (Temporary) (subclass 870) visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Apply online using ImmiAccount
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Apply online using ImmiAccount: If you apply on or after 22 April 2026, you must lodge an online application using ImmiAccount: Create an account or log in to ImmiAccount. Attach documents. Pay the application fee. If you cannot apply online due to a technical issue, please submit an ImmiAccount Technical Support Form. If technical support does not resolve the issue, we will consider allowing you to submit a paper application. Using our website and protections to your privacy. We take our obligation to protect your privacy seriously.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Apply online using ImmiAccount
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Apply online using ImmiAccount: We provide a secure online environment, but you can do more to ensure your personal safety online: Make sure you give us your contact details when you apply for your visa and tell us if they have changed. We may need to contact you directly, even if you have: nominated your sponsor's email address for all electronic correspondence. appointed your sponsor or someone else to receive your correspondence as your authorised recipient. appointed someone to give you immigration assistance. Protect your email account, passwords and ImmiAccount. Do not share them with anyone.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): After you apply
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), After you apply: We will let you know when we have received your application and documents. There may be other things you need to know and might need to do.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Importing your paper application
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Importing your paper application: Applicants who have submitted a paper application can import it into ImmiAccount. You can do this after you receive your acknowledgement letter. Importing your application into ImmiAccount gives you access to online services. This makes it easier to manage your application. You can use our online services in ImmiAccount to: attach supporting documents to your application. view messages we send you. update your details. view the status of your application. Follow these steps to import your application: Create a new ImmiAccount or log into your existing ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Importing your paper application
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Importing your paper application: See instructions on how to use ImmiAccount. Once you log in, import your application by entering your: application ID. date of birth. identity document number (ImmiCard, passport or Titre de Voyage number). For more information, see Apply and Manage your application in ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Status updates
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Status updates: We cannot provide updates on your application's progress within normal processing times. We will let you know if you need to give us anything more. Learn more about the processing times at the Parent visa queue release dates.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Send more information
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Send more information: We might also ask you to provide more information. If you submitted your application online or imported it into ImmiAccount, you can use ImmiAccount to upload more documents that you did not send with your application. Alternatively, you can send us additional documents using the Parent visa processing centre form.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Travel
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Travel: You must tell us if you want to travel outside Australia while we process your application. We need to know because you must be in Australia when we make our decision. If you leave Australia, make sure you have a valid visa to return. Learn about visa expiry.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Health exams
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Health exams: We will let you know when you need to complete health examinations.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Biometrics
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Biometrics: We might ask for biometrics (fingerprints and photo). We will let you know if you need to provide them.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Pay the second instalment
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Pay the second instalment: You must pay the second instalment before we will grant the visa. We will send you an invoice when it is due. If you do not pay the invoice, we will refuse your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Add family members
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Add family members: You might be able to add family members to your application before we make a decision. Complete and send us Form 1436 Adding an additional applicant after lodgement. If you have submitted your application online, or imported your application into ImmiAccount, you can use ImmiAccount to upload the form. Alternatively, you can send us the form using the Parent visa processing centre form. You will also need to give us evidence of your relationship and a copy of the family member's passport.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Add family members
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Add family members: If you want to add a spouse or de facto partner to your application, they can be in or outside Australia when you add them unless you applied as a retiree. If you applied as a retiree, your spouse or de facto partner must be in Australia when you add them. If you want to add a dependent child to your application, they can be in or outside Australia when you add them.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Newborn child
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Newborn child: Find out what to do if your child is born after you apply.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Mistakes on your application
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Mistakes on your application: Tell us as soon as you can if you make a mistake on your application. To do this, complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers. If you have submitted your application online, or imported your application into ImmiAccount, you can use ImmiAccount to upload the form. Alternatively, you can send us the form using the Parent visa processing centre form.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Help with your application
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Help with your application: Tell us if you no longer want someone to: receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. provide immigration assistance - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person. If you have submitted your application online, or imported your application into ImmiAccount, you can use ImmiAccount to upload the form. Alternatively, you can send us the form using the Parent visa processing centre form. For more information see Who can help you with your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Tell us if things change
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Tell us if things change: You need to tell us about changes to your: phone number. address. passport. relationship status. family composition, including the birth of a child. You should also tell us if you want to withdraw your application. See what to do if your situation changes.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Withdraw your application and apply for a different visa
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Withdraw your application and apply for a different visa: Other parent visas might be processed more quickly including the: Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143). This is a permanent visa. Contributory Parent visas may be processed faster, but it costs more than a Parent visa (subclass 103). Contributory Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 173) followed by a permanent Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143). This 2-step visa process is faster but costs more than the Parent visa (subclass 103). It also costs more than applying directly for the Contributory Parent visa (subclass 143), but the cost is spread across the 2 visas over a longer period.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Withdraw your application and apply for a different visa
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Withdraw your application and apply for a different visa: If you switch to one of these Contributory Parent visas, we will take the date you originally applied for a subclass 103 visa into account for your new application. Switching to a Contributory Parent visa application will not disadvantage you. Not all applicants who applied for the subclass 103 visa need to apply for a contributory visa. If one applicant for the subclass 103 visa changes their application, it will not affect the other application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Stay lawful
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Stay lawful: Make sure you stay lawful by holding a valid visa while we process your application. When you apply for this visa in Australia, we are likely to grant you a bridging visa. If your current visa expires before we make a decision on your application, the bridging visa will start. You can stay in Australia on the bridging visa while we process your new visa application. Do not cancel your current visa. If you do, you may: be staying in Australia unlawfully. not be eligible for a bridging visa. Learn more about visa expiry.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Visa outcome
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Visa outcome: New step description.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804): Visa outcome
abstract: Aged Parent visa (subclass 804), Visa outcome: You must be in Australia, but not in immigration clearance, when we make a decision on your application. We will let you know our decision in writing. If we grant you the visa, we will let you know: your visa grant number. the date your visa starts. your visa conditions. You should keep a copy of our decision. If we refuse your visa we will tell you: why we refused the visa. if you have a right to a review of the decision. We will not refund the application fee if we refuse your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): With this visa you can
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), With this visa you can: can visit Australia for up to 3 or 5 years per visa. can apply for further visas to visit up to a maximum period in Australia of 10 years. cannot work in Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): How long you can stay
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), How long you can stay: Up to 3 or 5 years.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Cost
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Cost: Up to 3 years. Up to 5 years. Concessions apply in limited circumstances. Cost concession. From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application. See About this visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): You must
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), You must: have an approved Parent Sponsor before you can lodge an application for this visa. apply online for this visa. lodge your visa application within 6 months of the sponsorship approval, or 60 days if we give you permission to apply in Australia. Permission to apply in Australia is only approved in limited circumstances. Help with your visa. If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Be eligible to apply
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Be eligible to apply: To be eligible to apply, you must: be the biological, legal (including adoptive) parent, step-parent or parent in-law of the Parent Sponsor. be at least 18 years of age. There is no balance of family test or Assurance of Support requirements for this visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Have a sponsor
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Have a sponsor: You must have an approved Parent Sponsor to apply for this visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Have met any previous visa obligations
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Have met any previous visa obligations: You must have met and complied with any previous visa obligations.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Meet the health requirement
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Meet the health requirement: You must meet our health requirement.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Meet the character requirement
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Meet the character requirement: You must meet our character requirement.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Have enough money
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Have enough money: You must have, or have access to, enough money to support yourself while you are in Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Have a genuine intention to stay in Australia temporarily
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Have a genuine intention to stay in Australia temporarily: You must intend to: stay only temporarily in Australia. do only the things the visa allows you to do. If you have already lodged a permanent parent visa application, you may visit Australia, but not remain in Australia permanently while the application is being decided. This is a temporary visa only. You will not have the right to permanent residence. You cannot apply for a permanent or temporary parent visa if you have applied for or hold this visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Health insurance
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Health insurance: You must have and maintain adequate arrangements for health insurance from an Australian Health Insurance provider to cover any unforeseen medical treatment you might need while you are in Australia. See what we consider adequate health insurance. Learn more about health insurance for overseas visitors. Reciprocal healthcare agreements. Some countries have a reciprocal healthcare agreement with Australia. Find out more from Services Australia about reciprocal healthcare agreements.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Have no debt to the Australian government
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Have no debt to the Australian government: If you owe the Australian Government money or you have a public health debt, you must have paid it back or have arrangements in place to pay it back.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Before you apply
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Before you apply: New step description.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Before you apply
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Before you apply: Before you apply, check you are eligible. Check that you have an approved Parent Sponsor. You can't apply for or be granted this visa if you do not have an approved Parent Sponsor.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Check your passport
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Check your passport: You must have a valid passport. We will only grant the visa if you have a valid passport.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Get help with your application
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Get help with your application: Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be: a registered migration agent. a legal practitioner, or. an exempt person. You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Gather your documents
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Gather your documents: New step description.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Gather your documents
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Gather your documents: Provide evidence to support your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Provide accurate documents
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Provide accurate documents: Provide accurate information. See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide accurate information.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Identity documents
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Identity documents: We need proof of your identity. If you cannot prove your identity: we will refuse your visa application. we might not grant you another visa for 10 years. Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates. Also provide: a national identity card, if you have one. proof of change of name.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Identity documents
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Identity documents: Documents that prove a change of name include: a marriage or divorce certificate. change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority. documents that show other names you have been known by such as a birth certificate showing the names of both parents or custody documents issued by the relevant court of law.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Permission to Apply in Australia
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Permission to Apply in Australia: We will tell your approved Parent Sponsor if you have Permission to Apply in Australia (but not in immigration clearance) if we approve their sponsorship. This advice will be provided in a Permission to Apply letter. You must attach a copy of this letter to your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Genuine intention to stay in Australia temporarily
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Genuine intention to stay in Australia temporarily: Give as much evidence as possible to show that you intend to visit Australia temporarily. This may include items that indicate your ties to your home country, your financial position and your planned activities while you are in Australia. A non-exhaustive list of examples include: Proof you have enough money for your stay and to leave Australia, for example: Itemised personal bank statements showing a 3-month period. Tax records. Pension or other regular income streams. Evidence of any previous international travel.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Genuine intention to stay in Australia temporarily
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Genuine intention to stay in Australia temporarily: Your ability and reasons to return home, such as: Any significant financial ties, such as a house, a business or other major assets in your home country. Evidence of ties or commitments to your home country, including any family. A letter stating your reasons and plans for visiting Australia. The letter could state: The purpose of your stay and any plans. Who you are intending to visit while in Australia and their relationship to you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Character documents
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Character documents: Provide an Australian police certificate if you have spent a total of 12 months or more in Australia in the last 10 years since you turned 16. We only accept complete disclosure National Police Certificates issued by the Australian Federal Police. We do not accept standard disclosure certificates or national police certificates issued by Australian state or territory police.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870): Character documents
abstract: Sponsored Parent (Temporary) visa (subclass 870), Character documents: Also provide: an overseas police certificate from every country, including your home country, where you spent a total of 12 months or more in the last 10 years since you turned 16. military service records or discharge papers if you served in the armed forces of any country. Complete and provide the following forms: Form 80 Personal particulars for assessment including character assessment.

You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.

abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Gather your documents: Include as much information as possible to support your application. This includes English translations of your documents. We may decide your application without requesting further information from you. Follow these instructions to ensure you submit a complete visa application.

title: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602): Medical treatment documents
abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Medical treatment documents: If you are applying for this visa to receive medical treatment or donate an organ, provide a letter from your treating doctor in Australia outlining: your medical condition. treatment that will be required. an estimate of the timeframe. an estimate of the cost involved. You will also need to complete Form 1507 Evidence of intended medical treatment (includes consultation) if: you are applying in Australia, and. you do not hold a substantive visa (a visa other than a bridging visa, criminal justice visa or an enforcement visa).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602): Identity documents
abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Identity documents: Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates. Also provide: a national identity card, if you have one. proof of change of name, if applicable, such as: a marriage or divorce certificate. change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority. documents that show other names you have been known by.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602): Additional documents for applicants under 18 years old
abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Additional documents for applicants under 18 years old: If you are under the age of 18, you should provide a copy of your birth certificate showing the names of both parents. If you can’t provide a birth certificate, provide identification pages from one of the following: a family book showing the names of both parents. an identification document issued by the government. a court-issued document that proves your identity. a family census register. If somebody other than your biological parents has legal guardianship over you (for example, adoptive parents or a court-appointed guardian), you must provide proof of their legal guardianship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602): Additional documents for applicants under 18 years old
abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Additional documents for applicants under 18 years old: Provide adoption papers or parental court orders, if applicable. Anyone with a legal right to decide where you live, and who is not travelling in Australia with you, must complete either: Form 1229 - Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years. a statutory declaration giving their consent for you to visit Australia on this visa. Include a document with the signature and photo of the person completing the form or declaration. This could be a passport or driver’s licence.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602): Additional documents for applicants under 18 years old
abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Additional documents for applicants under 18 years old: In addition to consent information, if you’re not staying with a relative or legal guardian, provide Form 1257 - Undertaking declaration. The person you’re staying with must sign the form.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602): Financial documents
abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Financial documents: We need proof that you have access to enough money to: pay for your treatment. support yourself and anyone who comes with you while you are in Australia. Provide: letters from any Australians who will be supporting you during your stay. a letter from your treating doctor or hospital saying they are satisfied with arrangements for payment.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602): Financial documents
abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Financial documents: If you are going to be treated in a public hospital, the letter about payment arrangements must: come from the financial officer or the administration department of the hospital. confirm that no Australian will be disadvantaged in accessing medical services as a result of your treatment.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602): Translate
abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Translate: Have all non-English documents translated into English. Provide original and translated documents in your application. Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters. Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their: full name. address and telephone number. qualifications and experience in the language they are translating. These details must be in English. Note: You do not need to have any documents certified unless we ask you to.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602): Scan or photograph
abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Scan or photograph: Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour. The scans and photos must be clear and legible. If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file.

abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Attach: Attach a document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing. Learn more about attaching documents.

abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Travel: If you applied in Australia, you must tell us if you want to travel outside Australia while we process your application. title: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602): Stay lawful
abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Stay lawful: If you are in Australia, you must stay lawful by holding a valid visa while we process your application. Don't let your current visa expire before you apply. If you do: you will be in Australia unlawfully. you might not be eligible for a BVA. Learn more about visa expiry.

abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Tell us if things change: Tell us if things change after you submit your application but before we have made a decision. title: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602): Visa outcome
abstract: Medical Treatment visa (subclass 602), Visa outcome: We will let you know our decision in writing. If you applied in Australia, you must be in Australia when we grant the visa. If you applied outside Australia, you must be outside Australia when we grant the visa. If we grant your visa, we will tell you: your visa grant number. the date your visa starts. the period that your visa will be valid for. your visa conditions, if applicable. Keep a copy of the decision with you when in Australia. If we refuse your visa, we will tell you: why we refused the visa. if you have a right to a review of the decision.
